title: The Current State of Browser Agents - Jerry Wu and Wyatt Marshall
talk_summary: A benchmark study of browser agents (WebBench, 5,000 tasks across ~500 sites) showing read tasks succeed ~80% while write tasks drop ~50%, with failures split between agent capability and infrastructure (captcha, proxy, login, timeouts). The practical advice is to pick read vs write use cases deliberately, test multiple browser-infra providers, and hybridize deterministic scripts with agents for long-tail steps.

takeaways.technique: Split failures into agent vs infrastructure buckets when scoring runs
takeaways.what_they_do: They classify every failed task as agent failure (should have been able to do it) vs infrastructure failure (framework/proxy/captcha/login blocked it), and report them separately so infra fixes are visible as a distinct lever.

takeaways.technique: Hybrid deterministic-script + agent for long-tail steps
takeaways.what_they_do: Production users run fixed Playwright-style deterministic flows for high-volume, stable steps and reserve the agent only for dynamic/long-tail steps, rather than making the agent do everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: using a mix of browser agents for tasks or workflows that are more long tail ... mixing that with more deterministic workflows such as playright

takeaways.technique: Pick use cases by read-vs-write difficulty before building
takeaways.what_they_do: They show read/information tasks are near-solved (~80%) while write/state-changing tasks halve in success, and advise choosing scope accordingly and testing write paths rigorously before production.
takeaways.evidence_quote: overall performance on write tasks is much much worse. Drops about 50% or more
takeaways.numbers: read ~80% success; write drops ~50%+; combined best ~2/3, average ~50%

takeaways.technique: Benchmark and swap infrastructure providers per use case
takeaways.what_they_do: They recommend testing multiple browser-infra providers because success swings materially by provider and site, and providers can unblock proxies on request.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the browser infra you choose can have pretty strong performance swings ... Try multiple providers

takeaways.what_they_do: They attribute write-task failures partly to longer trajectories (more steps = more chances to err) and flag long-context memory as the key fix for multi-step accuracy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: some right tasks take almost three times the amount of steps as retasks ... having longerterm context on how to execute those tasks will be incredibly important
takeaways.numbers: write tasks ~3x the steps of read tasks

takeaways.technique: Cap retries to avoid failure death spirals
takeaways.what_they_do: They note agents that can't recognize failure keep retrying until timeout, inflating latency and cost; the fix is detecting non-progress and stopping.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they just keep trying and trying and trying until they hit a timeout
